title: Critical Cisco Nexus 9000 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code as Root
content_md: Cisco has disclosed a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Nexus 9000 Series Switches equipped with Silicon One ASICs that could allow unauthenticated attackers to run arbitrary code with root privileges. Tracked as CVE-2026-20212, the flaw received a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.8 out of 10 and is documented in Cisco advisory cisco-sa-n9k-s1-rce-EH8dEtr. Cisco published the final advisory on September 2, 2026, and released software updates and temporary mitigations for affected customers. Critical Cisco Nexus 9000 Flaw The vulnerability exists in the Silicon One integration used by specific Cisco Nexus 9000 platforms. According to Cisco, TCP ports 43210 and 43211 are accessible through the default Layer 3 virtual routing and forwarding (VRF) instance. An unauthenticated remote attacker could connect to an exposed affected switch and send specially crafted input to these ports. Successful exploitation could result in attacker-supplied code being executed with root-level privileges on the device. Root access would give an attacker extensive control over the impacted network switch, potentially enabling configuration manipulation, credential collection, traffic interception, disruption of data-center connectivity, or use of the compromised device as a foothold for further network attacks.
